title: Prince Behram and Princess Al-Datma

keywords: prince behram and the princess al-datma
full_text:
Princess Al-Datma of Yemen was renowned across the Arabian peninsula for her extraordinary martial prowess, her agility with the javelin, and her unbending vow: she would marry only the suitor who could unhorse her in single combat with the lance, while every defeated suitor must surrender his horse, armor, and weapons to her armory.

Hundreds of proud emirs and champions had challenged her, and all had been tumbled into the dust by her lightning spear.

Prince Behram of Persia, hearing of her fame, traveled to Yemen. Seeing her noble bearing and skill, he resolved to court her not through brute force, but through agile strategy and chivalric courtesy.

They met upon the tournament field before thousands of spectators. For three hours their stallions circled, their lances clashing with sparks of iron, matching stroke for stroke with equal valor.

Perceiving that her defense was impenetrable to direct assault, Behram adopted a subtle stratagem: during an intense exchange, he feigned that his horse’s stirrup had snapped, leaning to the side with apparent vulnerability.

Al-Datma charged to deliver the decisive stroke. Quick as a leopard, Behram ducked beneath her lance, seized the rim of her shield with agile grace, and using her own forward momentum, lifted her gently from the saddle and set her upon her feet upon the turf without bruising a single hair!

He dismounted immediately, sheathed his sword, bowed low, and presented his own stallion’s reins into her hands as a token of reverence for her unmatched skill.

Princess Al-Datma, moved by his brilliant agility and peerless courtesy, smiled and gave him her hand, declaring that a champion who combines martial skill with chivalric honor is the only partner worthy of a warrior queen.
moral: Chivalric valor combined with humble wit wins what mere force and pride can never conquer.
